title: Request shaping, speculative prefix trimming, and hot-KV offload for OOM avoidance
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent OOMs on high-concurrency workloads where long conversational prefixes fill the GPU KV cache and large batches push per-GPU allocation beyond available memory. Existing mitigation (aggressive eviction + model fallback) either causes quality regressions or a hard outage.

Proposal summary: Implement a multi-pronged, low-risk runtime feature set that avoids hard OOMs while minimizing quality loss: 1) request shaping that admits/defers requests based on real-time memory pressure and expected token cost; 2) speculative prefix trimming driven by a token-importance heuristic to drop low-value prefix tokens instead of the most-recent context; 3) hot-KV offload that transparently moves cold KV entries to a compressed, host-pinned staging area while keeping hot entries on GPU; and 4) coordinated progressive fallback to lighter quantized variants only when offload and trimming cannot recover memory headroom. This initiative aims for graceful degradation (preserve recent context, reduce latency spikes) rather than abrupt failures.

Design notes: request shaping integrates with the admission controller to score incoming requests by estimated memory delta (prompt length, cached KV reuse probability). Speculative trimming runs before eviction: an importance scorer (fast transformer or lightweight heuristic using token type and recency) produces a mask of safe-to-drop tokens; trimmed tokens are stored as a compact delta (lossy small coalesced tokens) so we can rehydrate if later needed. Hot-KV offload uses a per-GPU LRU sampler to select cold KV shards and move them into a shared host pinned region using 4-bit compressed deltas and a lightweight index; on-demand prefetch will rehydrate the top-k most recently accessed shards. Offload is asynchronous and bounded by a per-GPU bandwidth cap to maintain latency SLOs.

Why different from existing work: prior tickets focus on eviction policies and model fallback. This ticket couples admission control, content-aware speculative prefix trimming, and a compression-backed host offload path to avoid both quality regressions and costly model swaps. The novelty is token-importance trimming + compact host-staging of KV with on-demand rehydration and an admission gate that reasons about expected memory delta.

Risks and trade-offs: trimming may remove context that matters for downstream quality; mitigation: conservative default thresholds, a fallback that can ask client to resend trimmed prefix if evaluation shows issues. Host offload adds complexity and CPU/PCIe bandwidth usage; mitigate with rate limits and tuned compression codecs. Admission shaping increases tail latency for deferred requests; mitigate with user-facing throttling and retries with exponential backoff.

Links: Design doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=design-hot-kv-offload-speculative-trim (internal). Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8923. Bench dashboards: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/memory-resilience
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype that performs hot-KV offload for cold shards and rehydrates on demand (benchmarked locally)
Speculative prefix trimming implemented with pluggable importance scorer and unit tests for correctness and rehydration
Admission controller can score requests and defer/queue them when estimated memory delta would exceed bounded headroom
Bench results: OOMs reduced by >= 90% on the internal synthetic long-prefix workload compared to baseline eviction-only strategy
Latency impact: 95th/99th token-generation latency increase <= 15% and p99 under customer SLO for top-tier customers on test workloads
Quality impact: end-to-end ROUGE/LM-eval or custom metric degradation <= 3% for representative prompts; flagged cases reviewed in eval runbook
End-to-end integration tests for offload + trimming + fallback preserved in CI with simulated memory pressure scenarios
plan: Phase 1 - Prototype (2 weeks): implement hot-KV offload prototype + simple trimming heuristic; smoke tests on single-GPU instances
Phase 2 - Bench & refine (2 weeks): microbench throughput/latency under realistic traces; iterate compressor settings and trimming thresholds
Phase 3 - Canary rollout (3 weeks): enable feature behind runtime feature flag on a small pool, collect metrics and customer signals
Phase 4 - Gradual traffic ramp (2 weeks): widen to more pools with adaptive thresholds and automated rollback triggers
Phase 5 - Postmortem & docs (1 week): finalize runbook, SDK opt-ins, and operational dashboards
metrics: OOM events per 1M requests (baseline vs feature-flagged)
p95 and p99 token generation latency
observed GPU memory headroom distribution during peak windows
rehydration cache hit ratio for offloaded KV shards
percent of requests trimmed and average tokens dropped per request
downstream quality metric delta on eval prompt set

2026-03-06 Priya Kapoor (PM): Please ensure we have a clear UX for SDK users when trimming happens (opt-in vs server-driven). I flagged possible API change; prefer server-side default with telemetry and an opt-out header.
2026-03-09 Liam Chen (SRE): Canary plan looks good. Add alert: 'rehydration-failure-rate > 1%' to trigger auto-disable. Also request a runbook entry for manual intervention steps.

2026-03-12 Diego Morales: Ran internal bench with conversation trace set A. OOM frequency dropped from 18/1M to 0/1M with offload+trimming. p99 latency increased by 11%. Pushing iteration to lower compression CPU cost.

2026-03-14 Asha Raman: Merged integration tests for simulated memory pressure. Next: expand trimming scorer from heuristic -> learnable fast scorer (ML-ops spike) depending on bench results. Scheduling a review with Design for user-visible messaging.
